cim: UNESCO, Brazilian Government and ITU partner to launch green AI Climate Institute
cim_eredeti: UNESCO, Brazilian Government and ITU partner to launch green AI Climate Institute
szoveg_eredeti:
Artificial intelligence holds immense promises for climate action—from forecasting extreme weather to tracking deforestation and optimizing freshwater resources. Yet across the Global South, the countries most vulnerable to climate disruption face structural barriers: restricted computing capacity, fragmented data governance and severe technical skills gaps. Compounding this challenge, the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure carries its own significant carbon, energy and water footprint.

To bridge these divides, UNESCO, the Government of Brazil and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) have formed a strategic partnership to establish the Artificial Intelligence Climate Institute (AICI). Announced at COP30[VL1] in Belém and now moving to full implementation, the Institute aims to provide developing nations with the institutional and technical capacity to design, deploy and govern their own ethical, resource-efficient AI solutions.

Anchored under ITU’s Green Digital Action Hub and institutionally hosted by Brazil’s National Telecommunications Agency (Anatel), AICI operationalizes Objective 4 of the COP29 Declaration on Green Digital Action—expanding digital inclusion, literacy and targeted skills development for climate resilience.

The initiative combines regulatory leadership, global technical standards and human-rights-based ethical governance into a shared operational model:

The foundational milestone took place on 11 November 2025 during COP30 in Belém, where the Institute’s vision was unveiled. The partners committed to a two-year operational roadmap (2026-2027) focused on country-led capacity building.

This roadmap translated into concrete action on 4 August 2026 in Manaus, Brazil, with an inaugural workshop “Infrastructure, Intelligence and Impact: the Pathway to a Sustainable Future.” Hosted by Anatel and the UNESCO Brasília Office, the event brought together regional regulators, digital policymakers, and multilateral development banks—to finalize AICI’s operational structure:

For UNESCO, the AI Climate Institute is particularly relevant because it connects two of the defining issues of our time: the rapid advance of artificial intelligence and the urgency of tackling climate change. A truly sustainable AI must also be inclusive, and its benefits must reach countries and communities with different levels of technological and institutional capacity.

On 16 November 2026, the founding partners will officially launch the AICI operational phase in Antalya. The event will unveil the approved 2026-2027 work plan, showcase scalable pilot applications—including AI-driven deforestation prevention in the Amazon Basin—and formally open membership to governments, research institutions and international financing partners committed to sustainable digital transformation.

This article is related to the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.
